 After a cloudy, breezy and at times wet Monday, somewhat better weather is ahead for Tuesday. You will want to enjoy the mildest day over at least the next 7+ days since we have the coldest stretch of the season up next!
 It's part of our next weather makers :
 Central New York's next weather makers 
After leftover cloud coverage with a risk for some sprinkles or minor light showers Monday night through dawn Tuesday, I am expecting clouds to mix with some partial sunshine at times Tuesday. High temperatures should be in the upper 50s to near 60 degrees! While it will be breezy with a sustained 10 to 20 MPH breeze with gusts to 30 MPH, it is likely not only our mildest day ahead, but likely our best day ahead as the weather gets progressively worse from Wednesday night onward.
For Wednesday, there will be some cloudy periods that will hopefully mix with some filtered sunshine during the afternoon before that next system arrives.
As mentioned before, a new system will begin to affect our areas Wednesday night around midnight with some widespread steady rain moving in. This rain will likely continue throughout Thursday alongside a raw day with temperatures no better than the lower to middle 40s. Temperatures may actually fall backwards into the upper 30s. While most spots in Central New York will see just a cold rain, the best chance for rain to change to snow will be over the Adirondacks and the Tug Hill Plateau. There is a chance for some wet snow over the hills south of Syracuse. 
The forecast from Thursday night onward through Saturday becomes somewhat uncertain. While we do know that it will be colder than average with the coldest air of the season and a gusty increasing breeze, we are not sure whether or not this storm system will still be close enough to produce widespread leftover snow and/or rain Thursday night through parts of the weekend or we just have a spray of flurries and sprinkles with some thin bands of steadier snow or rain showers south of Lake Ontario and the Finger Lakes. Regardless, it appears that high temperatures for Friday through the weekend will likely not be higher than the upper 30s to lower or middle 40s with lower wind chills. We will continue to watch this carefully.
 Here is my forecast for high temperatures for the next 7 days in Syracuse & how it compares to normal :
 Tracking my forecast high temperatures for Syracuse for the next 7 days & how it compares to normal 
The last time Syracuse had high temperatures in the lower 40s was April 20th (nearly 7 months ago)! After getting record warmth for the first part of November, we are certainly making up for that with the forecast ahead for the end of this week into early next week.
Back to the potential for snow and how typical that is, believe it or not, Syracuse on average receives its first accumulating snow (0.1" or more) on November 4th. In addition, higher elevations typically see it even earlier! The bottom line is that it is very common for Syracuse and all of Central New York to get snow this time of year. The thing that makes this a little unusual is that we just had the warmest first 6 days of November on record. So, the swing from that to what's next is certainly eyebrow raising!
It is still way too early to figure out potential amounts of accumulating snow between Thursday night and this weekend since there is a lot of uncertainty to how this system develops.
However, we do know it is going to be cold and breezy with at least some localized snow and rain showers. We will keep you posted.
